labctl.notes: HOST-NATIVE (de-bridged): VICE runs on the host, headless, no QEMU/QMP, no guest OS, no X, no exec channel. Frames VICE_SHM_PATH->shm (the same IFB1 wire format drawshm uses), keys vicectl + the shared us-layout keysym table, audio -sounddev wav -> FIFO. Launcher stations/vice-native/x11-runtime.sh; reset=relaunch restores the checkpoint in /data/vms/streamhost/stations/c128/sta/golden.vsf. Publishes the VDC (80-column) canvas, not the VICII: x128 has two canvases and VICE_NATIVE_SHM_CHIP=VDC is what picks it. The CP/M disk is attached to drive 8 by the launcher's restore command block; the visitor boots it by typing BOOT.

museum.blurb: Three computers in one case: an 80-column business machine, a Commodore 64, and a CP/M box with a second CPU. The one exhibit here that can show you CP/M — the operating system that ran the office before MS-DOS did.
museum.notes: Live streamhost tile. Emulator-in-captured-Linux BRIDGE tile: a captured Debian 13 (trixie) kiosk runs VICE (x128) emulating a PAL C128; streamhost captures the Linux framebuffer + AC97 audio exactly like every other tile. In VICE's SDL2 build the VDC 80-column output is a SECOND canvas — `-80col` makes it the visible one (and chooses the boot display); `-dualwindow` never becomes visible under a kiosk with no window manager. No -VDCdsize: the 1:1 window is 789x576 and fills the 800x600 X root, where the doubled one is 1578x1152 and is clipped even at 1920x1080. VICE bundles the C128 ROMs but not the CP/M system DISK, which is staged in-guest and attached to drive 8 ~10 s AFTER reset — the KERNAL boots any CP/M disk it finds at power-on, and this tile's fixture is the untouched BASIC 7.0 screen. The visitor types BOOT (one SPA keyboard button) to reach CP/M 3.0. No C64 button: GO64 works but paints the VIC-II while the visible VDC canvas freezes (measured — two byte-identical frames 10 s apart against a blinking-cursor control). Keyboard-only exhibit; beige-tower-crt fallback archetype. See streamhost/docs/BRIDGE.md and docs/guests/c128.md. HOST-NATIVE SINCE 2026-08-17 (de-bridging campaign): VICE x128 runs on the host, headless — no QEMU, no guest Debian, no X, and no in-guest attach helper. The published canvas is CHOSEN (VICE_SHM_CHIP=VDC), because x128 has two and the default would have shipped the 40-column VIC-II screen; the CP/M disk is attached to drive 8 in the same monitor command block as the checkpoint restore, past the KERNAL's boot-sector check. The prose above still describes the retired bridge tile and is rewritten with the other nine.

reset.fixture: Commodore 128 (PAL) 80-column power-on screen (BASIC V7.0, 122365 bytes free, READY.), HOST-NATIVE: VICE 3.10.0's x128 runs on the host, headless, and publishes the VDC canvas straight into the shm mapping at 856x576 native size. VICE_NATIVE_SHM_CHIP=VDC is what selects it, because x128 has a VICII canvas too and without the selector that one claims the mapping and the station would show the 40-column screen. No -VDCdsize: the bridged kiosk drew the VDC 1:1 in a 789x576 window on an 800x600 X root, so native size is the same glyph size the visitor has always seen, at a quarter of the encode cost of doubling. resetMode=relaunch: the launcher restarts x128, restores sta/golden.vsf through the monitor's own playback file, and ATTACHES THE CP/M 3.0 SYSTEM DISK to drive 8 in the same command block, at the READY breakpoint. That is already past the KERNAL's boot-sector check, which is why the disk can sit there unbooted without the in-guest attach helper the bridge tile needed. Restore verified at 856x576 with 8719 lit / 11263 non-dominant, the cold-boot gate's own numbers, nothing printed into BASIC. Route re-certified 2026-08-17 through the REAL SPA in a browser at the station's production pacing (60/60): PRINT 12+34 returns 46, and DIRECTORY lists the CP/M PLUS disk, which is what proves the attach end to end. GO64 was measured and deliberately NOT shipped as a button: it switches the machine to C64 mode on the VIC-II and freezes the visible VDC canvas. Keyboard-only exhibit (no mouse); SID sound -> FIFO.
